title: The Divergence Where Two Read Apart

features.name: split desk
features.desc-on-touch: Two reading surfaces that once faced each other now sit back-to-back. Each scholar learned to read without seeing the other's light.

features.name: diverging light
features.desc-on-touch: One lamp casts gold, the other cold white. The books between them learn to read by different suns, and their pages begin to argue.

features.name: separate margin notes
features.desc-on-touch: Annotations in two hands, reading the same text as two different stories. Neither hand quotes the other anymore.

features.name: angle of silence
features.desc-on-touch: The parent room taught them that reading was about angle of light. Here they learned: it was also about the angle of departure.

features.name: parallel questions
features.desc-on-touch: Each scholar asks the same question, but no longer to the same person. The answers begin to differ. They don't correct each other anymore.

features.name: where reflections end
features.desc-on-touch: Once their thoughts mirrored. Now you find the place where one scholar's question no longer reaches the other, where what was reflection becomes mere vicinity.

inscription: two readers in one light became one reader each, learning that understanding alone is a kind of loss

file.name: Letters_Unsent_Between_Scholars_Fragmentary.txt
file.note: Drafts written to each other but never delivered, arguments that stayed in margins, questions that were asked to books instead of to hands.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the study where angles began to differ
narr: In the same room, you read facing her at last.
Her eyes move faster than yours across the same page.
You find a passage that means something to you both.
But she's already interpreted it differently, alone.
The books between you stop being mirrors and become
the things that taught you how to be separate.

exits.label: back to the dwelling where reading was still mutual
upward to chambers where solitude is accepted
toward a study where other scholars have similarly parted
to a place where two paths finally stop crossing
